title: Downtown Laredo's Plaza Theatre Still Closed as Restoration Costs Climb Into the Millions
excerpt: The historic Plaza Theatre has sat dark for more than three decades. The city has approved millions for its restoration, signed a $1.7 million facade contract this year, and still has no opening date.
content:
The Plaza Theatre in downtown Laredo was already dark when Grand Theft Auto V came out on Sept. 17, 2013. More than 13 years later, with Grand Theft Auto VI arriving Nov. 19, 2026, the historic theatre at 1018 Hidalgo St. is still closed — and the city still has no opening date for it.

Built in 1947 in the Art Modern style, the 1,586-seat Plaza was once downtown’s showpiece. The City of Laredo acquired the theatre in 1999 with plans to restore it. It has now sat idle for more than three decades.

The money approved for the project has grown into the millions. By mid-2024, more than $12 million had been approved for the restoration, much of it not yet spent. Separately, U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar secured a $750,000 federal earmark for accessibility improvements, roof repairs, restroom code updates, light repairs and mural restorations.

The work has moved in phases. In December 2020, the council approved a $238,300 design contract with Able City LLC to assess the building and draw up a master plan. On Jan. 20, 2026, the council awarded a $1,723,333 construction contract to Zertuche Construction Texas LLC for the theatre’s envelope and facade enhancements, with 160 working days to complete the work and funding from the Capital Improvements Fund.

In February 2026, the council voted unanimously to restore the theatre to its original use as a working theatre, scaled to roughly $8.5 million — the amount available — rather than a larger multipurpose concept estimated at $17 million to $18 million. About $8.7 million remained available for the project, including the $750,000 in federal housing funds. City officials estimated the work would take about 18 months.

Even so, the main restoration has yet to begin. On Sept. 8, 2026, the council advanced the next step of the process, selecting three firms — Leyendecker Construction of Texas, Stoddard Enterprise and Midas Contractors — to submit proposals for construction management at-risk services for the Plaza Theatre Preservation and Restoration Project. As of late August, the project’s third phase was still in design, with construction not expected to begin before December 2026.

The council has also asked staff for a written update on the rehabilitation and for a study of whether the Plaza could serve as a civic center. For now, the marquee stays dark, and downtown’s most familiar theatre remains a restoration project with no opening date.

Sources: City of Laredo City Council agenda, Jan. 20, 2026; City of Laredo City Council agenda, Sept. 8, 2026; Office of U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar; ConstructConnect.
